resources.string: Night light data for any location: BMNT/EENT, sunrise/sunset, moonrise/moonset, moon illumination and an HLL/LLL stoplight for up to 90 nights. Computed on the device; works fully offline.
Tap the map or a marker to get illumination data there. Press Pick again to cancel.
No GPS position yet. Using the map center.

Clear-sky estimates from the USNO Circular 171 illuminance model (adjusted by the Sky setting). Cloud, terrain, smoke and cultural lighting change real light levels. Not a substitute for official SLAP or weather products.
Light standard, mission type, rated window, time zone

USAF (AFI 11-214): high illumination is at least 2.2 millilux, about a 20% moon at 30° or higher.
USN/USMC (MCO 3500.14): HLL is 0.0022 lux or above (the same threshold); planning tools ignore low moon angle, terrain and shadows.
Army: at least 23% illumination with the moon at least 30° up (rule of thumb; verify against your SOP).
Custom: your own numbers below.
Custom standard (when Service standard is Custom)

A night is solid HLL (High Light Level) when at least (100 minus this) percent of the window is HLL, and solid LLL (Low Light Level) when at most this percent is HLL. Anything in between is MIXED. Current:
Adds the USNO 0.5 millilux night-sky term. Off is more conservative for NVG planning.

Off = doctrine (flat terrain), as USAF/USN planning tools do. On = uses the DTED/SRTM elevation data loaded in ATAK to block moonlight while the moon is behind hills or ridges at the selected point. The doctrine rating is still shown next to the terrain rating. Bare earth only: trees and buildings are not included.

%s.\nAutomatic shows times as local time at the selected point: your device clock when the point is within 100 km of you, otherwise the military time zone for the point\u2019s longitude (no daylight saving). The zone is always shown above the times.

SS / SR: Sunset / Sunrise (upper edge of the sun on the horizon).
EECT / BMCT: End of Evening / Beginning of Morning Civil Twilight. Sun 6° below the horizon.
EENT / BMNT: End of Evening / Beginning of Morning Nautical Twilight. Sun 12° below the horizon. The default rated window runs from EENT to BMNT.
EEAT / BMAT: End of Evening / Beginning of Morning Astronomical Twilight. Sun 18° below the horizon (full darkness).
MR / MS: Moonrise / Moonset. “@ 071°” is the true azimuth where it rises or sets.
Illum: percentage of the moon’s disk that is lit. ↑ waxing (growing), ↓ waning (shrinking).
Moon max: highest the moon gets above the horizon inside the window.
Moonlight: brightest moonlight inside the window.
HLL / LLL: High / Low Light Level, at or above / below the selected standard’s threshold.
MIXED: part of the window is HLL and part is LLL. The notes list the HLL periods.
lux / mlux: units of illuminance. 1 mlux (millilux) = 0.001 lux. Full moon high in the sky: about 0.25 lux. HLL threshold: 2.2 mlux.
NVG: Night Vision Goggles. Degain: the NVG dims its gain when bright light (such as a low moon) is in view.
Letter after a time: the military time zone the time is in, e.g. Z = Zulu (UTC), R = UTC−5, D = UTC+4. An asterisk means an extra half hour (C* = UTC+3:30). The line above the times says which zone is in use. By default times are local at the selected point.
AO: Area of Operations.
AFI: Air Force Instruction. MCO: Marine Corps Order. SOP: Standing Operating Procedure.
Shadows: SHORT (moon high, 45° or more: shadows about as long as the object or shorter), MEDIUM (20–45°: up to about 3× the object), LONG (moon under 20°: long, dark shadows behind trees, buildings and terrain). Shadows point away from the moon. NVG glare: the moon is low in that direction; NVGs wash out looking toward it.
Terrain: with Factor in terrain on, the moon counts as hidden while it is behind the local skyline (from loaded DTED/SRTM, 20 km around the point). “Clears terrain” is when the moon actually reaches this spot. Doctrine ratings ignore terrain.
SLAP: the official military solar/lunar almanac data used in NVG briefs.
USNO: U.S. Naval Observatory, source of the illuminance model.
Timeline: shading = sky (day, civil, nautical, astronomical, night). Yellow top strip = moon up (dim = up but behind terrain). White line = estimated light (log scale). Dashed line = HLL threshold. Bottom strip = stoplight color. Cyan lines = rated window.
